MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Kansas (KU ScholarWorks hdl:1808/7996; open PDF via CORE 213394978). Supporting: Sagart, Laurent. 1999. Notes on Nanchang dialect (draft). catalog_locator: Sec. 1.1 'Tones, stress and syllable structure in Nanchang Chinese' and 1.1.1 'Lexical stress in Nanchang', pp. 2-3; sec. 1.1.2 'Grammatical stress in Nanchang', pp. 3-8 (closing statement p. 8); Abstract p. iv.
catalog_quote: Like in Standard Chinese, the lexical stress in Nanchang is realized on disyllabic words where the first syllable is a full syllable and the second syllable is a light syllable known as ‘qing sheng’ (Chao 1968). Perceptually, native speakers can tell that the first syllable is more prominent than the second syllable. ... In disyllabic words, only the second syllable can be lexically stressless. The presence or absence of lexical stress on the second syllable sometimes may distinguish the meanings of two words: (1a) toŋ42 ɕi42 ‘east west’ (1b) toŋ42 ɕi ‘thing’. In (1a), the syllables are “full-full” and it is not easy for native speakers to tell which has more stress. In (1b), the syllables are “full-light” and the first syllable is judged to be more stressed than the second syllable by native speakers. ... There is no rule that predicts whether a word will have a full-light structure in Standard Chinese or Nanchang. Therefore the stress pattern of full-light disyllabic words has to be lexically specified. The lexicon with a full-light pattern in Nanchang, however, is not the same as the lexicon of the same stress pattern in Standard Chinese. ... [p. 8] Based on these arguments, in Nanchang, a [V N] phrase has grammatical stress on N and a [N1 N2] compound has grammatical stress on N1.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nanchang Gan is a tone language (five citation tones). Word-level prominence is a full-syllable vs. light-syllable (qingsheng, toneless/reduced) contrast: a light syllable can only be the non-initial (second) syllable of a disyllable, giving strong-weak words, and which words have a light second syllable is lexically listed, not rule-governed; in full-full words speakers perceive no clear stress difference. Above the word, 'grammatical stress' follows Duanmu's Nonhead Stress: N1 is stressed in [N1 N2] compounds (initial), N in [V N] phrases (final), supported by speaker judgments, blocking of 213-tone sandhi on stressed N1, and longer rhyme durations (p. 8: 'in Nanchang, a [V N] phrase has grammatical stress on N and a [N1 N2] compound has grammatical stress on N1').
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; the thesis distinguishes three prominence grades instrumentally (grammatically stressed > lexically stressed but grammatically stressless > lexically stressless/light), with rhyme duration as correlate and tonal inventory reduced from 5 to 2 on light syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: Full-light membership is lexically idiosyncratic and differs from the Standard Chinese neutral-tone lexicon; checked (CVO) syllables are short regardless of stress; Sagart 1999 adds that lexicalized T0 items are typically grammatical morphemes and that restressing a T0 syllable yields tone 7; Sagart 1989 (Shanggao Gan) states an atonic syllable is never the first syllable of a polysyllabic morpheme.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level = disyllabic words (full vs light second syllable); compound/phrase level = Nonhead Stress ([N N] initial, [V N] final). Data are elicited disyllables in a carrier context plus native-speaker prominence judgments; variety is urban Nanchang.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes Nanchang city Gan (南昌话, the prestige/reference variety of Gan, Chang-Du subgroup); Glottolog treats Gan (ganc1239) at language level with Nanchang as its usual reference point. Supporting first-hand notes: Sagart 1999 (also Nanchang) and Sagart 1989 (Shanggao, Yi-Liu subgroup). Li Xuping 2018 (not opened) describes Yichun Gan (Yi-Liu subgroup). Zhang Shengkai's TUFS work is on Pingjiang (Hunan), a peripheral Gan variety.

new_statements.quote: When it comes to the analysis of tones in Nanchang Gan (NCG), I prefer to consider the nature of TBU as a syllable. Based on the auditory impression from me as a native speaker, the directionality of the strong stress (which is based on the intensity) is not consistent throughout the language. For example, [t͡ɕɛ ɸən] 'to get married' exhibits a right-strong stress foot, by having the second syllable [ɸən] strong, while some other words like [t͡ɕɛ pa] 'to stammer' are left-stressed. [...] it seems that the stress in NCG cannot be predicted by lexical categories. Therefore, it is hard to generalize stress in NCG as simply right/left-stress foot language, nor could the stress be a reliable predictor of the lexical categories in this language.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nanchang Gan is a tone language (five monosyllabic lexical tones; eight tones on compound-initial syllables; right-dominant tone sandhi in which the final syllable of a disyllabic compound keeps its citation tone and the first syllable changes). On stress the author, a native speaker, reports only an auditory impression: in disyllables the intensity-stronger syllable is sometimes the second ([t͡ɕɛ ɸən] 'to get married') and sometimes the first ([t͡ɕɛ pa] 'to stammer'); stress position is not predictable from lexical category and NCG cannot be classed as a uniformly left- or right-strong foot language. No placement rule is given; stress is set aside and tones are analysed per syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: No rule, hence no exceptions; the two example words are given as evidence that prominence side varies word by word. The author notes (sec. 2.1, p. 8) that her city-dialect data differ from Liu (2010) in syllable structure (no CVO/checked syllables found) and suggests the two studies may describe different varieties (city vs. town Nanchang).
new_statements.identity_note: Cai 2021 describes the Nanchang city dialect (author is the sole speaker, female, 25, born and raised in Nanchang city); she distinguishes it from the 'town dialect' of surrounding districts and suggests Liu (2010/2011) may describe a different variety (different syllable structure, CVO checked syllables absent in her data).

tone_statements.citation: 孙立新 (Sun Lixin). 2024. 陕西山阳县杨地赣语岛的语音特点及两字组连读变调 [Phonetic characteristics and disyllabic tone sandhi of the Yangdi Gan dialect island in Shanyang county, Shaanxi]. 甘肃高师学报 Journal of Gansu Normal Colleges 29(3): 28-33.
tone_statements.quote: 该方言岛有3个单字调，即平声阳去、上声、去声；根据连读变调推断，在迁出其祖居地之前最少有阴平、阳平、上声、去声、入声等5个单字调。
tone_statements.translation: This dialect island has 3 citation tones, namely ping/yang-qu, shang and qu; judging from tone sandhi, before leaving its ancestral home it had at least 5 citation tones: yin-ping, yang-ping, shang, qu and ru.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: 3 citation tones (a heavily merged Gan system) with sandhi preserving traces of a 5-tone stage.

tone_statements.citation: 曾玲 (Zeng Ling), 余俊毅 (Yu Junyi) & 刘新中 (Liu Xinzhong). 2022. 基于系统声学实验的赣语遂川话声调研究 [Tone features of the Suichuan Gan dialect based on acoustic data]. 中国语音学报 Chinese Journal of Phonetics 2022(1) [第17辑; issued 2021-12]: 56-67. 北京: 中国社会科学出版社 (ISBN 978-7-5227-0989-5).
tone_statements.quote: 研究发现，遂川话的上声分阴阳，去声不分阴阳，且保留入声调，与吉茶片大多数方言点存在差异。从具体的分化路径上看，古浊上归去声和阳上而非阴平；古清去不归阳平，并依声母送气与否分为两个调类，送气归入声，不送气归去声；古入声按清浊二分，清入为入声，全浊入归去声，次浊部分随清入，部分随浊入，与赣方言次浊入的分化大规律一致。
tone_statements.translation: We find that in Suichuan the shang tone splits into yin and yang, the qu tone does not, and a ru tone is retained, differing from most points of the Ji-Cha cluster. As to the paths of splitting: MC voiced shang goes to qu and yang-shang rather than yin-ping; MC voiceless qu does not go to yang-ping but divides into two categories by aspiration of the initial - aspirated to the ru tone, unaspirated to qu; MC ru divides by voicing: voiceless ru is the ru tone, fully voiced ru goes to qu, sonorant ru goes partly with voiceless and partly with voiced ru, in line with the general Gan pattern.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract (Chinese) in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Suichuan Gan: yin-ping, yang-ping, yin-shang, yang-shang, qu, ru (six categories implied), with aspiration-conditioned reassignment of MC voiceless-qu words.

tone_statements.citation: Jin Shajuan (金莎娟) & Xiao Jiugen (肖九根). 2020. The Characteristics of the Phonetic System of Shigang (Shangping) Dialect in Xinjian District, Nanchang [南昌新建区石岗(上坪)方言音系特点]. Science Innovation 8(1): 11-17. doi:10.11648/j.si.20200801.15
tone_statements.quote: 2.3．声调系统：除轻声外，有7个调类、8个调值 ... 表1 声调类型。 ... 阴平 ... 甲类 45 ... 乙类 445 ... 阳平 453 ... 上声 213 ... 阴去 33 ... 阳去 11 ... 阴入 5 ... 阳入 1 ... 声调说明： 1) 古全清平和次清平由声母是否送气而分调，[6](第188-211页）将其分为阴平甲、乙二类，且属高升调，阴平乙类调值前半段平调动程较长，后半段上升。 2) 古全浊上声今归为阳去。 3) 入声分阴阳，阴入调值高，阳入调值低。[7] 4) 去声多为平调，阴去为中平调，阳去为低平调。
tone_statements.translation: 2.3. Tone system: apart from the neutral tone there are 7 tone categories and 8 tone values ... Table 1 Tone types ... yinping ... type A 45 ... type B 445 ... yangping 453 ... shangsheng 213 ... yinqu 33 ... yangqu 11 ... yinru 5 ... yangru 1 ... Notes on the tones: 1) MC fully-voiceless and aspirated-voiceless ping-tone words split by whether the initial is aspirated; [6] (pp. 188-211) divides them into yinping A and B, both high rising; in yinping B the first half is a fairly long level stretch and the second half rises. 2) MC fully-voiced shang words now go to yangqu. 3) The entering tone splits into yin and yang: yinru is high, yangru low. [7] 4) The qu tones are mostly level: yinqu is mid level, yangqu low level.
tone_statements.locator: p. 13, sec. 2.3 声调系统 (表1 声调类型 + 声调说明) (table cells quoted in reading order)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Seven tone categories, eight citation values: yinping 45/445 (split by initial aspiration), yangping 453, shang 213, yinqu 33, yangqu 11, yinru 5, yangru 1; a neutral tone exists outside the count.

tone_statements.citation: 卢继芳 (Lu Jifang) & 张晓霞 (Zhang Xiaoxia). 2020. 赣语昌都片方言中古入声字今读特点与演变规律 [The characteristics and evolution of the modern pronunciation of MC rusheng-tone characters in the Chang-Du group of Gan]. 南昌大学学报 (人文社会科学版) Journal of Nanchang University (Humanities and Social Sciences) 51(2): 119-128.
tone_statements.quote: 昌都片赣语中古入声调类演变条件有声母清浊、古声母送气与否、韵摄来源。从地理分布来看,北部方言入声字舒声化进程快于南部方言;从语音系统内部来看,不同声母的入声字舒声化进程也有差异,大多数方言浊入字先于清入字发生舒声化演变,浊入声字舒声化演变以归向阳去调为常。
tone_statements.translation: In Chang-Du Gan the conditions on the evolution of the MC ru-tone category are voicing of the initial, aspiration of the MC initial, and rhyme-group origin. Geographically, ru-tone words lose their checked quality faster in the northern dialects than in the southern ones; system-internally the pace differs by initial: in most dialects voiced-ru words de-check before voiceless-ru words, and voiced-ru words most commonly merge into the yang-qu tone.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 119-128)
tone_statements.summary: Checked (ru) tones of Chang-Du Gan: yin-ru/yang-ru with further aspiration- and rhyme-conditioned splits, undergoing merger into yang-qu / yin-qu / yang-ping at different rates.

tone_statements.citation: 曹志耘 (Cao Zhiyun), 孙宜志 (Sun Yizhi) & 秋谷裕幸 (Akitani Hiroyuki). 2020. 江西南丰方言音系 [The phonology of the Nanfeng dialect, Jiangxi]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2020(2): 158-172.
tone_statements.quote: 南丰县位于赣闽交界,方言兼具赣客特点,古全浊声母逢塞音塞擦音今读送气清音,阳声韵和入声韵韵尾保留三分格局,入声字有[l]韵尾,发生了气流分调、韵尾分调等语音变化。本文描写南丰方言的声韵调系统,归纳其主要的音韵特点,编写同音字汇。
tone_statements.translation: Nanfeng county lies on the Jiangxi-Fujian border and its dialect combines Gan and Hakka features: MC voiced obstruents are read as voiceless aspirates, nasal and checked rhymes keep a three-way coda pattern, ru words have an [l] coda, and sound changes such as airflow-conditioned and coda-conditioned tone splitting have occurred. The paper describes the initials, finals and tones of Nanfeng, summarizes its main phonological features and provides a homophone syllabary.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record

tone_statements.citation: 习晨 (Xi Chen). 2019. 赣语樟树方言两字组中的轻声 [Neutral tone in disyllabic groups of the Zhangshu dialect (Gan)]. 文山学院学报 Journal of Wenshan University 32(5) [2019(5)]: 83-86.
tone_statements.quote: 通过收集樟树方言里轻声的语料,并对樟树方言的轻声进行分类,可以发现樟树方言中轻声情况比较复杂,兼有自主和非自主变轻声、调值和调类轻声。
tone_statements.translation: Collecting and classifying neutral-tone data from the Zhangshu dialect shows that neutral tone in Zhangshu is rather complex, including both autonomous and non-autonomous neutralization and both tone-value and tone-category neutral tones.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone with grammatically conditioned neutral tone in second syllables.

tone_statements.citation: 彭泽润 (Peng Zerun), 胡月 (Hu Yue) & 曹慧菊 (Cao Huiju). 2019. 湖南耒阳赣语的声调类型分布和官话化趋势 [The distribution of tone types and the trend toward Mandarin in the Gan dialect of Leiyang, Hunan]. 武陵学刊 Journal of Wuling 44(4): 101-105.
tone_statements.quote: 湖南耒阳方言属于赣语,但是在声调上,耒阳南部和东部的方言开始被官话同化。官话4个声调格局的特点已经从耒阳南部延伸到北部,靠近耒阳市区。古代入声在耒阳各地主体上被保留,但是古代浊音入声一般归属阴平。
tone_statements.translation: The Leiyang dialect of Hunan belongs to Gan, but tonally the dialects of southern and eastern Leiyang have begun to be assimilated by Mandarin. The Mandarin 4-tone pattern has extended from the south of Leiyang to the north, close to the city. The MC ru tone is on the whole retained across Leiyang, but MC voiced ru generally goes to yin-ping.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Geographic cline from a Gan system with a retained ru tone to a Mandarin-type 4-tone system.

tone_statements.citation: 朱磊 (Zhu Lei). 2016 [NCPSSD label 2016(1); publ. 2015]. 赣语余干方言入声的性质 [A phonetic and phonological analysis of Yugan checked-tone syllables]. 中国语音学报 Chinese Journal of Phonetics 第6辑: 46-52. 北京: 中国社会科学出版社 (ISBN 978-7-5161-9492-8).
tone_statements.quote: 调查表明,余干入声鼻尾占整个入声音节的比例较稳定,且承担了阴入和阳入的音高区别.但是,此鼻尾只出现在停顿前,且阳入字在停顿前也常常不带鼻尾;另一方面,在后接余干方言中唯一的高调阴去调时,入声会导致阴去变调,且阴去变成的调与入声单念时所带鼻尾的声调一致.
tone_statements.translation: The survey shows that the nasal tail of Yugan ru syllables occupies a fairly stable proportion of the syllable and carries the pitch distinction between yin-ru and yang-ru. But this nasal tail appears only before pause, and yang-ru words often lack it even there; on the other hand, before yin-qu, the only high tone of Yugan, a ru tone causes yin-qu to change, and the resulting tone is identical to the tone carried by the nasal tail of the ru tone in isolation.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record
tone_statements.summary: Yin-ru vs yang-ru distinguished by the pitch of a pre-pausal nasal release (floating tone); yin-qu is the only high tone.

tone_statements.citation: 李冬香 (Li Dongxiang). 2016. 湖南赣语古入声的演变 [On the evolution of the checked tone in the Gan dialects of Hunan]. 广东技术师范学院学报 Journal of Guangdong Polytechnic Normal University 37(4): 28-35.
tone_statements.quote: 根据湖南赣语18个方言点的材料指出,湖南赣语有的有入声调,有的没有入声调。无论是有入声调的方言还是无入声调的方言,其内部又可分为不同的小类。
tone_statements.translation: On the basis of material from 18 Hunan Gan dialect points it is shown that some Hunan Gan dialects have a ru tone and some do not; both the dialects with and those without a ru tone can be further divided into sub-types.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record

tone_statements.citation: 冉启斌 (Ran Qibin), 顾倩 (Gu Qian) & 余慧敏 (Yu Huimin). 2015 [publ. 2014-11]. 进贤七里赣语有多少个声调?——汉语方言极限声调清单声学实验分析之二 [How many tones in Jinxian (Qili) Gan? The acoustic analysis of extreme tone inventories across Chinese dialects, II]. 中国语音学报 Chinese Journal of Phonetics [NCPSSD issue label 2015; 辑 number not verified]: 28-40. 北京: 中国社会科学出版社 (ISBN 978-7-5161-2816-9).
tone_statements.quote: 按《汉语方言地图集》江西进贤七里乡赣语声调达13个之多;但在其他报道中与七里仅10余公里之隔的县城却仅有6—7个声调,两地差异何以如此巨大?本文使用"极限类别"声调例字设计法,通过声学分析看到两地声调系统仍然具有内在一致性,分歧的原因主要在于"送气分调"程度的不同.
tone_statements.translation: According to the Linguistic Atlas of Chinese Dialects the Gan of Qili township, Jinxian, Jiangxi has as many as 13 tones; yet in other reports the county town only some 10 km from Qili has just 6-7 tones - why so large a difference? Using the 'extreme category' tone word-list design, acoustic analysis shows that the two tone systems are still internally consistent and that the divergence lies mainly in different degrees of aspiration-conditioned tone splitting.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract (Chinese) in the NCPSSD record; English abstract also present
tone_statements.summary: Jinxian Qili Gan: 12-14 surface tone categories produced by aspiration-conditioned splitting of the basic 6-7 categories; the split is receding in the county-town variety.

tone_statements.citation: 昌梅香 (Chang Meixiang). 2012. 赣语遂川方言的送气分调 [Tone variation of qusheng with aspirated consonants in Suichuan Gan]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2012(4): 310-313.
tone_statements.quote: 赣语遂川方言古清声母去声字按今声母送气与否分为两个调类，这与很多送气分调的赣语相同。但遂川方言与其他赣语不同的是，部分擦音h、f、e、s，边音l，鼻音m、n,η、日及零声母字，其声调与送气的清声母去声字相同。
tone_statements.translation: In the Suichuan dialect of Gan, MC qu-tone words with voiceless initials divide into two tone categories according to whether the present-day initial is aspirated, as in many Gan dialects with aspiration-conditioned tone splitting. What distinguishes Suichuan from other Gan dialects is that part of the words with the fricatives h, f, e[ɕ], s, the lateral l, the nasals m, n, ŋ, the MC ri initial and zero initial have the same tone as the aspirated voiceless-initial qu-tone words.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 310-313)
tone_statements.summary: Aspiration-conditioned split of the yin-qu category into two tones, with sonorant/fricative/zero-initial words partly joining the aspirated class.

tone_statements.citation: 吴小奕 (Wu Xiaoyi). 2011. 监利方言古阴平字声调的特殊表现 [Special evolution of the old yinping tone in the Jianli dialect]. 语言研究 Yuyan Yanjiu (Studies in Language and Linguistics) 31(2): 96-101.
tone_statements.quote: 赣语监利方言古阴平字的单字调分化为两类：一类是所有阴声韵尾及少量阳声韵尾字，仍保持本调；另一类是大部分阳声韵字，其单字调调型和调值变得与当地入声相近。
tone_statements.translation: In the Jianli dialect of Gan the citation tone of MC yin-ping words has split into two classes: one, all words with open-syllable rhymes and a few with nasal rhymes, keeps the original tone; the other, most nasal-rhyme words, has taken on a contour and pitch value close to the local ru tone.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Rhyme-conditioned split of the yin-ping citation tone (nasal-final words approaching the ru tone).

tone_statements.citation: 周海霞 (Zhou Haixia). 2011. 牛蹄赣语两字组连读变调的音系学解释 [A phonological account of disyllabic tone sandhi in Niuti Gan]. 安康学院学报 Journal of Ankang University 23(6): 17-20.
tone_statements.quote: 牛蹄乡隶属于安康市汉滨区，是清初湖广移民造成的赣语方言岛。牛蹄赣语两字组连读变调的情况比较复杂
tone_statements.translation: Niuti township belongs to Hanbin district, Ankang, and is a Gan dialect island created by Huguang migration in the early Qing. Disyllabic tone sandhi in Niuti Gan is rather complex ...
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record

tone_statements.citation: 曹志耘 (Cao Zhiyun). 2011. 湖北通城方言的语音特点 [Phonological characteristics of the Tongcheng dialect, Hubei]. 语言研究 Yuyan Yanjiu (Studies in Language and Linguistics) 31(1) [2011(1)]: 106-112.
tone_statements.quote: 论文描写湖北通城麦市方言的声韵调系统，归纳其主要的音韵特点，并讨论若干重要的语音演变现象，包括：次清声母和全浊声母的关系，全浊声母的弱化，溪、群母的读音，入声韵尾的演变，气流分调，等等。
tone_statements.translation: The paper describes the initials, finals and tones of the Maishi dialect of Tongcheng, Hubei, summarizes its main phonological features and discusses several important sound changes, including the relation between MC voiceless-aspirated and voiced initials, weakening of voiced initials, the readings of the 溪 and 群 initials, the development of entering-tone codas, airflow-conditioned tone splitting, etc.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record

tone_statements.citation: 栗华益 (Li Huayi). 2011. 江西余干方言的入声韵尾 [Entering-tone endings in the Yugan Gan dialects, Jiangxi]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2011(1): 57-65.
tone_statements.quote: 入声调因喉塞鼻尾而产生特殊调值,并随着喉塞进一步弱化、消失而变化。
tone_statements.translation: The ru tones take on special tone values because of the glottal-stop-plus-nasal coda, and change as the glottal closure further weakens and disappears.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record

tone_statements.citation: 王晓君 (Wang Xiaojun). 2010. 江西新余方言的轻重音和轻声 [Stress and neutral tone in the Xinyu dialect, Jiangxi]. 中国方言学报 Zhongguo Fangyan Xuebao (Journal of Chinese Dialectology) 2 [NCPSSD: 2010(1)]: 100-111. 北京: 商务印书馆 (ISBN 978-7-100-06770-6).
tone_statements.quote: 新余方言的双音节词汇普遍存在轻重音,一般读作重轻型.轻声是由于轻重音的存在而产生的.轻声的调值主要由轻声字字调和该词语的方言融合度决定的.
tone_statements.translation: Disyllabic words in the Xinyu dialect generally have a light/heavy stress contrast, normally read heavy-light. The neutral tone arises from the existence of this stress contrast. The pitch value of the neutral tone is mainly determined by the citation tone of the neutral-tone syllable and by the degree of dialectal integration of the word.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone plus trochaic word stress; stress-induced neutral tone whose value depends on the syllable's own tone and lexical integration.

tone_statements.citation: 肖放亮 (Xiao Fangliang). 2010. 南昌县（塘南）方言语音系统 [The sound system of the Tangnan dialect of Nanchang county]. 江西科技师范学院学报 Journal of Jiangxi Science & Technology Normal University 2010(2): 39-42.
tone_statements.quote: 南昌县（塘南）方言是南昌方言的一种次方言。塘南方言的语音系统，由19个声母、62个韵母、7个声调构成。
tone_statements.translation: The Tangnan dialect of Nanchang county is a sub-dialect of Nanchang. Its sound system consists of 19 initials, 62 finals and 7 tones.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: 7 tones (values in the article body).

tone_statements.citation: 李军 (Li Jun) & 陈昌芳 (Chen Changfang). 2008. 19世纪中叶南昌话韵母与声调系统的特点 [Features of vowels (finals) and tones in the Nanchang dialect in the mid-19th century]. 广西师范大学学报 (哲学社会科学版) Journal of Guangxi Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences) 44(2): 58-63.
tone_statements.quote: 成书于清同治年间的南昌童蒙识字课本《类字蒙求》中的直音韵母、声调系统具有多方面的特点。这些直音所反映的语音系统与现代南昌话基本一致,也有一些差异。这些差异反映了一百多年来南昌方言的发展与演变。
tone_statements.translation: The homophone-gloss finals and tone system of the Nanchang children's literacy primer Leizi mengqiu, compiled in the Tongzhi years of the Qing, have several notable features. The sound system these glosses reflect is basically the same as modern Nanchang, with some differences; these differences reflect the development of the Nanchang dialect over more than a hundred years.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 58-63)

tone_statements.citation: 曾莉莉 (Zeng Lili). 2007. 丰城方言的轻声和连读变调 [Neutral tone and tone sandhi in the Fengcheng dialect]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2007(2): 119-123.
tone_statements.quote: 本文考察丰城方言的轻声和两字组连读变调。考察结果显示：轻声有高中低三种调值,且落在后字上,主要由前字调决定,与后字调无关。变调出现在前字上,当前字调为上声、去声、阴入时,在特定的条件下产生连读变调。无论轻声还是变调都与语法结构有关。
tone_statements.translation: This paper examines the neutral tone and disyllabic tone sandhi of the Fengcheng dialect. Results: the neutral tone has three values, high, mid and low, falls on the second syllable and is mainly determined by the tone of the first syllable, unrelated to the second syllable's tone. Sandhi appears on the first syllable: when it is shang, qu or yin-ru, sandhi arises under specific conditions. Both neutral tone and sandhi are related to grammatical structure.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone; right-hand neutral tone with 3 context-determined values; left-syllable sandhi for shang/qu/yin-ru.

tone_statements.citation: 邵宜 (Shao Yi). 2006. 赣语宜丰话词汇变调的类型及其表义功能 [On the types and functions of the lexical tone changes of the Yifeng dialect (Gan), Jiangxi]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2006(1): 38-44.
tone_statements.quote: 宜丰话词汇层面的声调有两种变异形式：表示小称的岛升变调和表示名词属性的高平变调。
tone_statements.translation: At the lexical level Yifeng has two forms of tonal variation: a high-rising [岛升 = misprint for 高升] changed tone expressing the diminutive and a high-level changed tone expressing noun-hood.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone plus two morphological changed tones (high-rising diminutive, high-level nominal).

tone_statements.citation: 龙安隆 (Long Anlong). 2006. 赣语永新话的两字连读变调 [Disyllabic tone sandhi of the Yongxin dialect (Gan) in western Jiangxi]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2006(1): 45-49.
tone_statements.quote: 赣语永新话连读变调的特点是同一种语音类型中分多种变调格式，大体上可看出与构词有关。
tone_statements.translation: The characteristic of tone sandhi in Yongxin Gan is that a single phonological (tonal) type divides into several sandhi patterns, which can broadly be seen to relate to word formation.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone with structure-sensitive disyllabic sandhi.

tone_statements.citation: 龙海燕 (Long Haiyan), 王铁山 (Wang Tieshan) & 黄小平 (Huang Xiaoping). 2006. 湖南省洞口县赣方言声调的比较研究 [Comparative research into tone in the Gan dialect of Dongkou county, Hunan]. 红河学院学报 Journal of Honghe University 4(1): 55-58.
tone_statements.quote: 首先把洞口县赣方言的声调和中古时期的汉语声调作纵向对比，探讨它们之间的对应关系和演变规律。其次把它与江西赣方言吉安片的声调和现代普通话的声调进行横向比较
tone_statements.translation: First the tones of the Dongkou Gan dialect are compared longitudinally with the Middle Chinese tones to explore their correspondences and rules of development; then they are compared laterally with the tones of the Ji'an cluster of Jiangxi Gan and of modern Standard Chinese.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record

tone_statements.citation: 蒋平 (Jiang Ping) & 谢留文 (Xie Liuwen). 2004. 古入声在赣、客方言中的演变 [The development of the MC entering tone in the Gan and Hakka dialects]. 语言研究 Yuyan Yanjiu (Studies in Language and Linguistics) 24(4): 71-78.
tone_statements.quote: 第一，古入声调在这些方言中的演变受声母清浊的影响．古全浊声母字的入声调一般归去声或阳去，古清声母的入声调在江西中西部和湖南东部一般归阴平，在江西北部归阴去。
tone_statements.translation: First, the development of the MC ru tone in these dialects is affected by the voicing of the initial: ru words with MC fully voiced initials generally join qu or yang-qu; the ru tone of MC voiceless-initial words generally joins yin-ping in central-west Jiangxi and east Hunan, and yin-qu in north Jiangxi.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record

tone_statements.citation: 李菡幽 (Li Hanyou). 2002. 赣语泰和方言阴平分两调 [The split of the yinping tone into two tones in the Taihe dialect (Gan)]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2002(3): 232-235.
tone_statements.quote: 赣语泰和方言阴平分化为两调,这一分化不受古四声清浊及今声母送气与否的影响,而是和韵类有关.
tone_statements.translation: In the Taihe dialect of Gan the yin-ping tone has split into two tones; this split is not affected by the voicing of the MC four tones nor by aspiration of the modern initial, but is related to rhyme class.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD search record
tone_statements.summary: Rhyme-class-conditioned split of yin-ping into two citation tones.

tone_statements.citation: 蒋平 (Jiang Ping) & 谢留文 (Xie Liuwen). 2001. 南昌县（蒋巷）方言的轻重音与变调 [Stress and tone sandhi in Nánchāng (Jiǎngxiàng) dialect]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 2001(2): 152-160.
tone_statements.quote: 考察结果显示:(一)重读音节除上声外总是保持单字调.(二)变调有两种.一种受调类限制,不受重音支配.这种变调只限于上声.另一种受重音支配的变调只出现在轻读音节里.(三)从'重轻轻'格式里尾字和中字不同的变调情况可以分辨两种不同的轻声:'边缘轻声'和'过渡轻声'.'过渡轻声'比'边缘轻声'更轻.
tone_statements.translation: The results show: (1) stressed syllables, except shang-tone ones, always keep the citation tone; (2) there are two kinds of tone change: one is restricted by tone category and not governed by stress - this sandhi is limited to the shang tone; the other, governed by stress, appears only in lightly-read (unstressed) syllables; (3) from the different sandhi behaviour of the final and the middle syllable in the 'heavy-light-light' pattern two different neutral tones can be distinguished, 'peripheral neutral tone' and 'transitional neutral tone'; the transitional one is lighter than the peripheral one.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 152-160)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone plus a stress (heavy/light syllable) contrast; category-conditioned sandhi limited to shang tone; stress-conditioned tone reduction in light syllables with two degrees of neutral tone.

tone_statements.citation: 辛世彪 (Xin Shibiao). 1999. 赣方言声调的演变类型 [Types of tonal evolution in the Gan dialects]. 暨南学报 (哲学社会科学版) Journal of Jinan University (Philosophy and Social Sciences) 21(3) [1999(3)]: 17-28.
tone_statements.quote: 本文比较了７５个方言点的材料，发现赣语声调数目有３、４、５、６、７、８、９、１０八种，但只有送气分调、浊上、去声和入声的变化与其声调演变类型之间存在本质的联系，据此可以归纳出赣语声调演变的１２种类型。
tone_statements.translation: This paper compares material from 75 dialect points and finds that the number of tones in Gan comes in eight sizes - 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 - but only aspiration-conditioned tone splitting and the changes of the voiced shang, the qu and the ru tones are essentially connected with the type of tonal evolution; on this basis 12 types of Gan tonal evolution can be set up.
tone_statements.locator: author abstract in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 17-28)
tone_statements.summary: Gan dialects have 3 to 10 tones; 12 diachronic tone-system types defined by aspiration-conditioned split and the reflexes of MC voiced shang, qu and ru.

tone_statements.citation: 陈昌仪 (Chen Changyi). 1992. 余干方言入声调的不连续成分 [The discontinuous component of the entering tones of the Yugan dialect]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 1992(2): 125-127.
tone_statements.quote: 江西省余干县城话的入声调类有两个特色,其一是入声韵在发了塞音尾之后,有一个短暂的间隔,然后有一个同部位的鼻音
tone_statements.translation: The ru tone categories of Yugan county-town speech have two peculiarities; the first is that in ru rhymes, after the stop coda is produced there is a short gap and then a homorganic nasal ...
tone_statements.locator: opening paragraph as carried in the NCPSSD record
tone_statements.summary: Checked tones realized in two parts (stop + pause + nasal), each with its own pitch.

tone_statements.citation: 熊正辉 (Xiong Zhenghui). 1979. 南昌方言的声调及其演变 [The tones of the Nanchang dialect and their evolution]. 方言 Fangyan (Dialect) 1979(4): 275-283.
tone_statements.quote: 南昌话有七个声调,平去入各分阴阳,上声不分阴阳。上声有连读变调,其余六调都不变调。从调类的演变看,南昌话的特点是声母的送气或非送气影响调类分合。同是古平声全浊声母宇,“头虫墙”今读送气声母,是[?]24调;“烦蛇嫌”今读非送气声母,是[?]35调。同是古去声清声母字,“痛菜秤”今读送气声母,是[?]213调;“布冻寄”今读非送气声母,是[?]35调。
tone_statements.translation: Nanchang has seven tones: ping, qu and ru each divide into yin and yang, shang does not. Shang has tone sandhi; the other six tones do not change. In terms of tone-category evolution, Nanchang's characteristic is that aspiration vs non-aspiration of the initial affects the splitting and merging of tone categories. Among MC ping-tone fully-voiced-initial words, 头虫墙, now read with aspirated initials, are tone 24; 烦蛇嫌, now read with unaspirated initials, are tone 35. Among MC qu-tone voiceless-initial words, 痛菜秤 (aspirated) are tone 213; 布冻寄 (unaspirated) are tone 35. ('[?]' = tone-letter glyphs lost in the database record.)
tone_statements.locator: author abstract as carried in the NCPSSD record (article pp. 275-283; sec. 壹 '南昌话的声调系统')
tone_statements.summary: 7 citation tones (yin/yang ping, shang, yin/yang qu, yin/yang ru) with aspiration-conditioned category assignment (e.g. yangping 24 vs 35-merger; yinqu 213 vs 35); sandhi restricted to shang tone.

readall_conflicts: No hard conflict. Liu (2011, existing statement) describes lexical stress in Nanchang as trochaic full-syllable + light-syllable (qingsheng) words, as in Standard Chinese; Cai (2021, sec. 2.2 p. 9) says that by native-speaker auditory impression the intensity-strong syllable in disyllables is sometimes the first and sometimes the second and cannot be generalized as left- or right-strong, while tone sandhi is right-dominant (sec. 2.3). The two are compatible if Liu's claim is restricted to qingsheng words; read as general claims about disyllables they pull in different directions (Liu: initial prominence; Cai: no consistent side, tonal stability on the final). Cai herself flags (p. 8) that her city-dialect data and Liu's may represent different Nanchang varieties. Neither source gives a fixed word-stress rule; both treat Nanchang as a tone language.

sources.citation: Liu, Jiang. 2011. Durational Properties of Lexical Stress and Grammatical Stress in Nanchang Chinese and Their Implications for Tonal Contrasts. MA thesis, Department of Linguistics, University of Kansas (hdl:1808/7996).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: Like in Standard Chinese, the lexical stress in Nanchang is realized on disyllabic words where the first syllable is a full syllable and the second syllable is a light syllable known as 'qing sheng' (Chao 1968). Perceptually, native speakers can tell that the first syllable is more prominent than the second syllable. [...] In disyllabic words, only the second syllable can be lexically stressless. [...] In (1a), the syllables are "full-full" and it is not easy for native speakers to tell which has more stress. [...] There is no rule that predicts whether a word will have a full-light structure in Standard Chinese or Nanchang. Therefore the stress pattern of full-light disyllabic words has to be lexically specified.
sources.locator: Sec. 1.1.1 'Lexical stress in Nanchang', pp. 2-3; Sec. 1.1.2, p. 8

sources.citation: Cai, Yu. 2021. Lexical and Sandhi Tones in Nanchang Gan: A Phonetic Description. MA thesis, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: When it comes to the analysis of tones in Nanchang Gan (NCG), I prefer to consider the nature of TBU as a syllable. Based on the auditory impression from me as a native speaker, the directionality of the strong stress (which is based on the intensity) is not consistent throughout the language. For example, [t͡ɕɛ ɸən] 'to get married' exhibits a right-strong stress foot, by having the second syllable [ɸən] strong, while some other words like [t͡ɕɛ pa] 'to stammer' are left-stressed. [...] it seems that the stress in NCG cannot be predicted by lexical categories. Therefore, it is hard to generalize stress in NCG as simply right/left-stress foot language, nor could the stress be a reliable predictor of the lexical categories in this language.
sources.locator: Ch. 2 Background, sec. 2.2 'Tone Bearing Unit (TBU)', printed p. 9 (p. 18); tone inventory sec. 2.1 pp. 7-8; sandhi directionality sec. 2.3 pp. 9-12

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.1.1-1.1.2 (pp.2-8): Nanchang is a tone language (5 tones); 'lexical stress' = full vs light (qingsheng) syllables; in disyllables only the 2nd syllable can be lexically stressless, first syllable judged more prominent; full-full words: speakers cannot tell which is more stressed; full-light pattern not predictable, lexically specified; 'grammatical stress' by Duanmu's Nonhead Stress: N stressed in [V N] phrases, N1 in [N1 N2] compounds (supported by speaker judgments, tone-sandhi blocking and rhyme-duration measurements); tonal inventory reduced to 2 in stressless syllables.

tone.translation: We find that in Suichuan the shang tone splits into yin and yang, the qu tone does not, and a ru tone is retained, differing from most points of the Ji-Cha cluster. As to the paths of splitting: MC voiced shang goes to qu and yang-shang rather than yin-ping; MC voiceless qu does not go to yang-ping but divides into two categories by aspiration of the initial - aspirated to the ru tone, unaspirated to qu; MC ru divides by voicing: voiceless ru is the ru tone, fully voiced ru goes to qu, sonorant ru goes partly with voiceless and partly with voiced ru, in line with the general Gan pattern.
